decisions.issues: Clean. Matches the beat: dusk hill under mango trees, a low two-tiered tiled gateway near the crown, the stone stair, a small party of torch-bearing Nair guards and horses with nobody readable as a rider, no banners or palanquin, no painted text. The open dusk sky across the upper left and centre gives plenty of room for both captions.

Acceptable with minor misses. Varma's knot sits high at the back of the crown rather than clearly above his LEFT ear. The sandal-paste line on his brow is not visible. His seat on the horse is a little ambiguous because the mundu hides his leg. Ramayyan wears a tiny ear stud that his sheet does not show. Everything else holds: Varma is bare-headed with no crest or spear, wears pearl drop earrings and one gold chain, and has a cream mundu with a gold border. Ramayyan has his receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, and looks up at the king. No text. The dusk sky at the upper centre-left holds both balloons.

Acceptable with minor misses. A faint thin orange vertical stroke at the centre of Nagoji's brow could read as a sandal mark, and the script asks for no forehead mark. It is about 3 px wide and almost invisible at reading size. Varma's face is a little rounder and younger than in panels 2, 4 and 5. His hair is wavy, with the knot at the back of the head rather than clearly above the LEFT ear. His single gold chain is a plain rope where the neighbouring panels show beads, and his brow has no sandal line. The dismount is caught mid-motion: he is still in the saddle, leaning forward with his bare foot out of the stirrup reaching down, not swinging a leg over. Some Nair guards stand up on the stair, and the gateway sits closer than in panel 1. Everything else holds and fixes the r1 failures. Varma is bare-headed with pearl drop earrings, one gold chain and a cream gold-bordered mundu, with no crest, spear or turban. He passes the reins to the turbaned stable boy while looking away. The heir, about ten, sits mounted behind on his own horse with wide watchful eyes, a topknot and a thin gold chain. Nagoji is at the right edge of the torchlight: high topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, silver chain, plain cream shoulder cloth. A long pale scar runs along his left forearm, with no dark sigil, and he is unarmed and uninjured. No text, no gore. The open dusk sky in the upper left is clear for Varma's balloon.

Acceptable. The sandal-paste line on Varma's brow is not visible, and he has a cream cloth over one shoulder (still bare-chested, not forbidden). Otherwise strong: Varma's profile matches the varma-v1 face study, with hair tied in a knot behind the left ear, a pearl drop earring, one gold chain, no crest and no spear. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) and faces the king closely. The Nair guards stand behind them. No text. The upper-left sky and foliage above Ramayyan hold both balloons without touching faces.

Acceptable with minor misses. Varma's knot sits at the back of his head, with loose curls at the nape, rather than clearly above the LEFT ear (panel 2 has the same). Below Nagoji's topknot, his hair hangs in loose curls to the shoulders. His pale scar runs from the upper arm across the elbow, not only along the inner forearm. Lettering room is only fair. Varma's balloon can sit over the dark foliage at upper left, between his head and the torch flames. Ramayyan's long balloon fits the sky and palms across the top centre-right, but it is pinched by Nagoji's head and may overlap the edge of the distant gateway. Otherwise strong, and the r1 failures are fixed. Varma has a lean face consistent with panels 2 and 4, black hair tied back, a pearl drop earring, a white sandal line on his brow, one beaded gold chain and a cream gold-bordered mundu, with no crest, spear or turban. He stands on the left, turned toward Ramayyan. Ramayyan stoops mid-bow in the middle, head turned toward Nagoji: receding curly hair, thin features, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Nagoji waits at the right edge of the torchlight: high topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, silver chain, plain shoulder cloth, no brand blot, unarmed and uninjured. The Nair guards are settled with their torches at the foot of the lit stair, with horses and a stable boy behind. Hands are sound, and there is no text or gore.

Minor: Varma's hair is mostly loose curls, with only a loosely gathered mass above his LEFT ear standing in for the side knot. He wears a vertical white namam where the script asks for a horizontal sandal line. Over-the-shoulder framing, Nagoji's topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud and silver chain, the pearl drops and single gold chain, and the dusk torchlit stair setting all match. The two balloons fit in the sky and canopy at upper centre, between the two heads.

Minor: this is a medium close-up, chest up, not a tight face close-up. Otherwise it is clean: thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, high topknot, tiny flush stud, no forehead mark, and a wry, almost-smile expression. The caption fits in the clear dusk sky at upper left.

Minor: a torch is mounted on a post at frame left, where the setting asks for no posts. Varma's knot sits at the back of his crown and is not clearly above the LEFT ear, which is turned away from camera. Varma and the heir carry namam marks rather than a sandal line. The beat reads well: Varma climbs ahead looking up at the bare rock, the heir is at his side, and Nagoji follows behind, unarmed, with the scar showing on his inner left forearm. The balloon fits over the night sky and grey rock face at upper centre.

Minor: Varma's hair is a topknot on the crown, not a side knot (this matches page 1 panels 1.2 and 1.4). Varma and the heir stand beside the jackfruit tree rather than directly under it, and they face camera rather than the sanctum; the boy's eyes do turn up-left toward it. The lingam inside is clearer than 'faintly'. Every other script element is present: the jasmine-hung sanctum, lamp niches in the peeling lime-wash, the roots heaving the flags, the cropped-hair assistant with a torch and a basket of ghee pots, and the sleeping dog. The long caption fits over the plain foreground stone at bottom left, or over the stone floor at bottom centre-right.

Minor: Varma's face is a little rounder and younger than the varma-v1 sheet. He wears a vertical namam rather than a sandal line. This is the best match of the page for the side knot: it sits above his LEFT ear with a pearl drop below. His hand rests soundly on the heir's shoulder as he turns toward off-panel right with a sly half-smile. The boy keeps his palms pressed, with eyes wide toward the doorway. The marks on the lingam are three ash stripes, not pseudo-text. The long balloon fits over the night sky and mandapa roofline at upper centre, or the plain lime-washed wall below it.

Minor only. The long white scar is drawn on the upper arm near the elbow rather than along the forearm next to the brand. The brand itself is a correct pale puckered patch on the inner LEFT forearm with no letters. The old priest's cloth has orange-red border stripes, while panel 3.2 shows his hands with a cream cloth and a gold border. Nagoji's topknot sits loosely on curly hair but reads as a crown knot. Varma has black hair, a pearl earring and is stooping at the sanctum. The heir is in a white mundu with a topknot. The lingam is ash-marked. There is clear night sky and leaves across the top middle for both captions.

Minor only. In the old priest's inset his cloth has a gold border, but panel 3.1 shows orange-red border stripes, a small costume mismatch. The out-of-focus lingam in inset 3 has textured ash stripes that only read as faint marks at high zoom; at print size they read as ash. Inset 1's wrist is walking along the steps rather than clearly down them. The four insets are correct: bangled wrist, cropped-hair bare-chested assistant with torch, priest's hands with wick and ghee lamp, sleeping dog. There is dark sky in the upper part of inset 1 for the caption.

Minor only. The chaver has a small red vertical mark through the three ash stripes, which the close-up in 3.4 does not show. Otherwise correct: young and clean-shaven with an ordinary face, low nape knot, white cloth over the LEFT shoulder, sacred thread, brass plate with flowers and clay lamp, no dagger. He steps out of the lit side-room door with his gaze off the left edge, and the sanctum is out of view. There is clear night sky at the upper left and middle for the caption.

Minor only. This extreme close-up fills the strip, so the whole head is larger than the frame; the face circle encloses the eyes and stripes only. The hair at the temples falls loose and curly rather than oiled back, and the red mark seen in 3.3 is absent. The eyes are still, unblinking and looking toward the left, lit warmly from below, with three thick ash stripes. Both captions must sit in the dark corners: top or far left (background and hair) and top or far right (hair and shadow), clear of the eyes and stripes.

Screen direction, setting and lighting are right. The chaver is on the left walking left, eyes down, cloth over his LEFT shoulder; niche-lamp flames bend while the plate flame burns straight up. Nagoji under the tree on the right is on model: high topknot, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain. But the chaver carries a large, clearly visible sheathed dagger tucked at his waist. That contradicts the hidden blade, which only appears from beneath his cloth in 4.2, and the beat that every detail of him looks correct. The two men are also half a frame apart, not within arm's length.
decisions.correction: Keep the setting, night lamplight, both costumes and the screen direction: the chaver on the LEFT walking left toward the sanctum, brass plate in both hands, eyes down and not looking at Nagoji; Nagoji on the RIGHT under the jackfruit tree, high topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, silver chain, unarmed. Remove the dagger entirely: no hilt, sheath, knife or dark object at the chaver's waist or anywhere in the picture. His waist cloth is smooth and plain. Bring the two men within arm's length: the chaver passes directly in front of Nagoji, only a single step between them, with Nagoji's head turned toward him, lips slightly parted as he speaks softly. Keep the niche-lamp flames bending and the plate flame straight up. Leave the dark sky and the upper tree trunk above their heads clear for a speech balloon near Nagoji and a short caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the chaver's mouth is nearly closed rather than visibly speaking; Varma and the boy wear a vertical namam rather than a horizontal line of sandal paste; the lamp on the plate is brass rather than clay; the boy stands mid-courtyard rather than right at the sanctum threshold. Faces, costume, three-figure count, setting (jasmine sanctum left, peeling lime-wash wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree right) and the dark upper sky/wall for the balloon and two captions are all sound.

Acceptable with small deviations: the chaver shows light stubble along the jaw (script says clean-shaven), bushier hair than in 4.1, and no ash stripes on his arm; the dagger is held reverse-grip at his hip pointing down rather than laid back along the forearm; Nagoji wears a plain silver bangle on his right wrist and carries the same heavy grey at the temples as on page 3. The beat is clear: plate, flowers and clay lamp falling, dagger in the chaver's left hand, Varma (black hair, side knot, pearl earrings, one gold chain, no crest or spear) planted with arms wide, the heir behind him, Nagoji launching by the tree. No painted text.

Minor only. The temple assistant has three ash stripes on his brow, a sacred thread and a white cloth over one shoulder, but his figure tag says no ash and no shoulder cloth. He is still clearly identified by the torch, his close-cropped hair and his open shouting mouth. Varma's hair is loose and curly with faint grey highlights and a knot near the crown on his left side, not a sleek side knot. This matches how he is drawn in the 4.2 frame. Everything else fits the beat: the shot is from behind the chaver (white cloth over his left shoulder, knot at the nape, sacred thread), the assistant hurls himself in from the mandapa side with the torch raised and hides the blade completely, Varma stands braced with his arms wide (pearl drops, one gold chain, moustache), and the jasmine sanctum is at left with the jackfruit tree at right. There is no text, blood or anachronism. The dark sky at top centre is clear for the 'Shiva!' balloon.

The generator painted the inset as a small bordered box in the upper-left corner of an otherwise empty wide courtyard. That is a painted panel border, and the actual beat (the assistant's silhouetted fall with the torch rolling) fills less than a fifth of the frame. Placed as the 4.4 inset, the frame would show an empty courtyard.
decisions.correction: Draw this as one single full-frame image with no inset box, no frame within the frame, no border line and no wider empty courtyard around it. The whole picture, seen low at floor level, is the dark silhouette of the bare-chested, close-cropped temple assistant crumpling onto the worn stone flags, knees buckling and one arm folding under him, backlit by niche-lamp glow. His torch has fallen from his hand and rolls across the flags in the foreground, its flame spilling a streak of orange light over the stones. Show the fall only: no wound, no blood, no dagger, no other figure. Keep the night palette, the wet-looking worn flags and a hint of a pillar base and a niche lamp behind him.

decisions.issues: Nagoji clamps the dagger wrist with his RIGHT arm, which comes from his right shoulder with his chest facing the viewer, and the brand and long scar are painted on that right forearm. The script and the injury continuity need his LEFT hand on the wrist (that palm is cut at 5.4), with the brand only on the inner LEFT forearm. The chaver wears a brown sleeveless vest and a maroon sash with loose curly hair, unlike the white-clad, nape-knotted temple man of 3.3 to 4.2. Nagoji's face, topknot, grey temple streak, gold stud and silver chain, the dog and the setting are good.
decisions.correction: Nagoji must clamp the chaver's dagger wrist with his LEFT hand. Stage the chaver on the left lunging toward screen left, toward the sanctum, his body turned partly to the viewer with the dagger in his LEFT hand nearest the viewer. Draw Nagoji crashing in from the right edge, seen from his left side, so the arm nearest the viewer is his LEFT arm, shooting forward from his LEFT shoulder to lock his left hand around the chaver's LEFT wrist, while his LEFT shoulder drives into the chaver's ribs and his right arm stays back behind his body. The pale puckered brand and the long white scar appear only on that LEFT inner forearm, never on his right arm. The chaver must look exactly as in the previous panels: young, lean, clean-shaven with no stubble, three horizontal ash stripes on the brow, oiled black hair in a tight knot low at the nape, bare-chested with a sacred thread, a plain white cloth wrapped at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder. NO brown vest or tunic, NO maroon sash. Keep the night courtyard with the jasmine-hung sanctum at left and the jackfruit tree at right, Nagoji's face, high topknot, grey temple streak, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, the dog bolting and barking in the background, and the dark sky at the top clear for a short caption.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): setting, lighting, Varma (bare chest, one gold chain, pearl drop earring, cream mundu, no spear) and the heir all match. The priest is wrong, though. He is a black-haired man of about thirty-five. In panel 3.1 and the MUST MATCH line he is the grey-haired old priest at the sanctum lamps, so readers would take this man for a second, unknown person. He also does not catch or haul the boy: he peers from behind a pillar at the right edge with his arms folded across his chest, and the boy's hand never reaches him. That pillar is on the struggle and tree side, so the boy is being sent toward the fight instead of back toward the sanctum. Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown, not above his LEFT ear.
decisions.correction: Fix the old priest and the direction of the shove; keep everything else that worked (the night courtyard, sanctum doorway with jasmine and faint lingam at screen LEFT, peeling lime-washed wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree at screen RIGHT, Varma's bare chest, one thin gold chain, pearl drop earring and cream gold-bordered mundu, the heir's look and wide staring eyes, clear wall and sky in the upper middle for the captions). The old priest must be visibly ELDERLY and the same man seen lighting the sanctum lamps earlier: grey-white hair tied in a knot, a lined, thin face from the temple priest sheet aged by thirty years, a slight stoop, white shoulder cloth with a gold border. He stands at a stone mandapa pillar at screen LEFT, on the sanctum side, with BOTH arms reaching out and actually gripping the boy, pulling him in behind that pillar. Varma is at centre-right, his body half turned toward the struggle off panel to the RIGHT, one arm swung back so his hand on the boy's shoulder shoves the boy LEFTWARD to the priest. His black hair is in a side knot above his LEFT ear. The boy stumbles leftward into the priest's hands, head twisted back over his shoulder, still staring right toward the unseen fight. No other figures; nobody stands between the boy and the right edge.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Nagoji is on the right and matches his sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, high topknot with grey at the temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth. His LEFT hand is locked on the chaver's dagger wrist with the dagger trembling between them. The chaver on the left is clean-shaven, with ash stripes, sweat and bared teeth. There is no painted text and no blood. Minor: the chaver's costume and hair do not follow the script (ochre torn sleeveless top, red sash and loose long curls, instead of white cloth over the left shoulder, a sacred thread and a knot at the nape). This does match his brown top and red sash in 4.3 and 4.5. The brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm is a small dark round stamp-like mark next to the white scar, not a pale puckered patch, but it has no readable letters. Caption space: the sky and wall top along the upper band, plus the leaves at upper right or the floor and roots at lower right.

v01 (the only candidate): Nagoji's look is right (moustache, clean chin, gold stud, topknot with grey temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth), and the chaver's elbow into his ribs reads well. But there are two daggers. The chaver holds a curved dagger free in his near hand at his waist, while Nagoji's left hand grips a different wrist at the bottom centre: a second fist holding a second hilt with a gold pommel. The real blade is therefore uncontrolled, which breaks the beat ('his left hand still on the wrist'), and the chapter's single-dagger rule. The chaver has also lost his ash stripes. The brand on Nagoji's forearm is a dark omega-like glyph that could read as a letter.
decisions.correction: Exactly ONE dagger and exactly four hands in the picture. The chaver (on the LEFT) holds his single dagger in his RIGHT hand, the hand nearer the viewer, and Nagoji's LEFT hand is clamped around THAT same right wrist, pinning the blade low and pointing away from both bodies. Draw no second hilt, second knife or extra fist anywhere, and nothing in Nagoji's right hand. The chaver's LEFT arm is the one bent sharply, its elbow slamming into Nagoji's ribs under the chest; that left hand is empty. Nagoji (on the RIGHT) folds around the blow, grimacing, his right arm close to his side. Keep the chaver clean-shaven with no moustache and give him back his three thick white horizontal ash stripes across the forehead. Draw the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm only as a pale, puckered patch of raised scar ridges beside the long white scar: no dark ink, no symbol and no letter-like shape. Keep everything else: the night courtyard with the sanctum and jasmine at screen left and the jackfruit tree at screen right, the niche lamps, Nagoji's topknot with grey temples, gold stud, silver chain and cream mundu with gold-bordered shoulder cloth, the chaver's ochre sleeveless top and dark red sash, and the clear night sky and wall in the upper part for the caption.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): wrong cast. The attacker holding the dagger on the left has Nagoji's captivity look: thick moustache, gold ear stud, long loose curls, torn ochre tunic and bandaged wrists. He is not a clean-shaven chaver. The figure on the right, with a pearl drop earring and a gold bead necklace, is Varma, and he is the one gripping the attacker's wrist. Ananthan Pillai (topknot with grey temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth) is missing entirely, so Nagoji's LEFT hand dragging on the chaver's wrist is not shown. The panel reads as Nagoji attacking the king. It also breaks screen direction: Varma should come in from the left (6.1, 6.3) with Nagoji on the right.
decisions.correction: Draw exactly THREE men, with no doubles. LEFT: Marthanda Varma, with the face, moustache and heavier build from his sheet, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, ONE thin gold chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a thin gold border, no turban, no crest, no spear. He steps IN toward the blade, weight driving forward, front foot advancing, hands rising, calm and set; he does not lean back. CENTRE: the chaver, a young, lean, wiry stranger, CLEAN-SHAVEN with NO moustache, NO ear ornament and NO wrist bandages, three thick white horizontal ash stripes across his forehead, short dark curly hair, in the same ochre sleeveless top, dark red sash and white lower cloth as the previous panels. He thrusts his single dagger upward, its point aimed at Varma's throat a hand-span short of it, never touching it. RIGHT: Nagoji as Ananthan Pillai: high Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu with a gold-bordered shoulder cloth, bare arms, no bandages, never the torn ochre captivity tunic. His LEFT hand is locked on the chaver's dagger wrist, dragging it back toward the right. The dagger is the only blade, and there is no blood. Keep the night courtyard with the sanctum and jasmine at screen left, the niche lamps on the peeling lime-washed wall, the jackfruit tree at screen right and the warm lamplight.

decisions.issues: v01 is the wrong beat and has no chaver at all. Only two men are drawn. Varma holds the dagger himself and drives his hand into NAGOJI's throat, while Nagoji grips Varma's wrist, so it reads as the king attacking Nagoji. Varma's hair is a bun on the crown, not a side knot above his LEFT ear. The courtyard, lamps, tree and Nagoji's look (moustache, grey temples, silver chain, stud) are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Draw THREE men, not two. The chaver, the assassin, stands in the CENTRE and holds the only dagger. He is young, lean and wiry, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, with three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead and oiled black hair tied in a tight knot low at the nape. He wears white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder, plus a thin sacred thread. His dagger arm thrusts up toward Varma. Varma is at screen LEFT, inside the dagger's arc: face from the varma sheet, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, one gold chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a thin gold border, and no weapon. His left hand clamps the CHAVER's forearm. His right hand drives stiff-fingered into the CHAVER's throat in a kalari strike, with a calm, practised face. Varma never holds the dagger and never touches Nagoji. Nagoji is at the right edge: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, high topknot, grey temples, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth. His LEFT hand stays locked on the chaver's dagger wrist just below Varma's grip, and he is not being struck. Keep this version's courtyard, niche lamps, sanctum at left, jackfruit tree at right and the open dark sky in the upper centre for one long caption.

decisions.issues: The head-butt beat and Varma's reel are well staged, but the chaver is drawn with a fully SHAVED head and a rudraksha mala, with no sacred thread and no shoulder cloth. Next to the curly-haired, nape-knotted chaver of 6.4 and 6.5 he reads as a different man. Varma's forehead mark is a set of vertical namam lines, not the horizontal sandal-paste line, and it is not shown smeared or broken. His hair knot sits at the back of the head rather than above his left ear.
decisions.correction: The chaver must keep his hair: oiled curly black hair tied back in a tight knot low at the nape, never a shaved or bald head. He is young, lean and wiry, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, with three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead. He wears a thin white sacred thread across the chest (no rudraksha beads) and white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder. Varma's forehead mark is a single HORIZONTAL line of pale sandal paste across the brow, visibly smeared and broken by the impact, never vertical namam lines. His black hair is in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with pearl drop earrings and one gold chain. Keep this version's composition: the chaver at left snapping his forehead into Varma's brow, Varma reeling back a step at right, the courtyard, niche lamps and jackfruit tree, and the clear upper wall and sky for two captions. No blood.

decisions.issues: The chaver has a moustache and stubble beard, a cloth headband, an ochre shirt and a red sash, which contradicts the clean-shaven, bare-chested chaver in the script and in 6.4. Varma has grey hair at the temples (forbidden: black hair only) and vertical namam marks instead of a smeared sandal-paste line. Nagoji's hair is loose with no high topknot and no grey at the temples. The dagger points at Varma's cheek, not under his jaw.
decisions.correction: The chaver in the middle is young, lean and wiry and fully CLEAN-SHAVEN, with no moustache, beard or stubble. He wears no headband, no shirt or tunic and no red sash. He is bare-chested with a thin sacred thread and wears white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder. He has three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead and oiled black hair tied in a tight knot low at the nape. Varma at the left edge has fully BLACK hair with no grey anywhere, tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, and a single horizontal line of sandal paste across his brow, smeared. He wears pearl drop earrings and one gold chain. The dagger's point drives toward the soft flesh UNDER his jaw and stops a hand-span short. Nagoji on the right wears his hair gathered in a HIGH TOPKNOT on the crown with first grey at the temples, not loose. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a tiny gold ear stud and a silver chain, and his RIGHT hand is just arriving to join his LEFT on the chaver's wrist. Keep this version's left-to-right staging, the courtyard, the lamps and the tree.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. The chaver wears a red waist sash where the bible gives white cloth. The lamplight falls more from the side than from below. Nagoji's brand sits on the top of his left forearm rather than the inner side. Otherwise clean: Nagoji on the right has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a gold stud, a high topknot, grey temples and a silver chain. The chaver on the left is clean-shaven with ash stripes and a knot at the nape, and the faces are inches apart with arms tangled high on the dagger. The two captions can sit top-left over the mandapa lintel and top-right over the sky.

Minor only. The chaver is young and clean-shaven, with three smeared ash stripes, hair tied at the nape and white cloth over his LEFT shoulder. The courtyard (sanctum left, niche lamps, jackfruit tree right) matches the page. His eyes show white all round small irises rather than blown pupils, so the look edges slightly toward fright, though the open grin reads as fierce joy. The face is rendered softer and more painterly than the inked neighbouring panels. The dark sky upper right gives clear room for the two short balloons, away from the face.

Acceptable. Nagoji is on the right and matches his sheet and the ch22 row: high topknot, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth with a gold border. His forehead snaps into the clean-shaven chaver's cheekbone and the chaver's head recoils, with no injury drawn. The room and lighting match page 6. One minor deviation: the chaver wears a long-sleeved tan shirt with a brown sash and loose curly hair, and no ash stripes show. The script tag calls for a bare chest, white cloth, a knot at the nape and ash stripes. Neighbouring panels draw him inconsistently anyway. The short caption can sit top left on the shrine entablature or in the dark sky and wall at the top centre and right.

Acceptable. It follows the r1 correction. The screen direction holds: the chaver is on screen LEFT in a white waist cloth with a rust-brown sash end, and Nagoji is on screen RIGHT in a white mundu with a gold border hem. The chaver's heel splashes and skids through the glossy oil smear. Nagoji's bare foot pushes in behind the chaver's heel and ankle. The tipped clay lamp is still burning, and crushed jasmine and red flowers lie in the oil. The shrine and lingam are at left and the jackfruit tree at right, all at night. There is no text or blood, and the visible feet are anatomically sound. Minor: the hook reads as Nagoji's toes and forefoot pressing behind the heel rather than a full instep curl, but the trip still reads. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji is slammed prone on the flags with his near (RIGHT) shoulder on the stone and his right arm crumpled under him. His left hand is flat, palm down and clean. His face is contorted. He matches the sheet and the ch22 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, grey temples, a topknot bun on the crown, the silver chain, and a white shoulder cloth and mundu with a gold border. The chaver tumbles on top of him, teeth bared. He is clean-shaven, with three white ash stripes, a sacred thread and a white cloth over his shoulder. The dagger is still in his hand, which feeds 7.4. The setting matches the page: sanctum and lingam at left, niche lamps, the side door, the jackfruit tree at right, night. Minor: the chaver's knot sits at the back of the head rather than low at the nape, and he keeps the rust-red sash seen in 6.4 and 7.2. The caption fits in the dark sky at top centre, above the wall.

The chaver in the background has a full moustache and beard; he must be clean-shaven. Nagoji braces himself on his RIGHT hand, but from 7.3 his right arm hangs useless. Both men are drawn fairly sharp rather than out of focus. Spired, pinnacled towers rise above the shrine roof at the top centre, close to the forbidden tall tower. The dagger composition itself is good: large in the foreground, resting against the foot of the pillar in a pool of niche-lamp light on the wet flags.
decisions.correction: Keep the low, floor-level wide shot with the dagger large and sharp in the foreground, resting against the foot of the stone pillar at screen right in a pool of niche-lamp light, the wet flags, and the shrine with its jasmine garland at screen left. Fix four things. (1) The chaver in the background is CLEAN-SHAVEN with NO moustache and NO beard. He is young and lean, with three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead and black hair tied back in a tight knot low at the nape, bare-chested with a white waist cloth and a white cloth over his LEFT shoulder. Acceptable. The r1 failures are fixed. Nagoji is now in ch22 dress: bare-chested with a cream shoulder cloth with a gold border. v01 (only candidate): the beat is wrong. The chaver is missing, and Nagoji lies on his back under Varma in the chaver's place, raising the dagger from below, so it reads as Varma pinning Nagoji. decisions.correction: Three separate men must be in the frame. 1) The chaver: young, lean, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, three thick horizontal ash stripes across his forehead, oiled hair in a low knot at the nape, white waist cloth. He lies pinned on his back on the flags, arching his bare chest upward toward the dagger's point, eyes fixed on the steel. 2) Varma, kneeling over the chaver at left centre with his RIGHT shoulder bearing down on the chaver's chest: fully BLACK hair with no grey, side knot above his LEFT ear, smeared sandal paste across the brow, one gold chain, pearl drop earrings, cream mundu with a thin gold border. 3) Nagoji, apart from them on the RIGHT side of the frame, up on ONE KNEE and not lying down or under anyone. His right arm hangs limp at his side and the dagger is raised high in his LEFT fist above the chaver's chest. Nagoji must never be the man pinned under Varma. Keep the courtyard (sanctum with jasmine at screen left, lamp niches, jackfruit roots at right), the warm lamplight and open upper wall and sky for two captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. This is a tight insert of Nagoji's LEFT forearm and hand coming in from screen left, with the cream shoulder cloth at the edge. The palm side faces the camera: fingernails curl toward us with the thumb over the guard, five digits, sound anatomy. On the inner forearm the brand is now a pale puckered patch of raised scar ridges with a thin white scar beside it. It is not a tattoo or symbol and has no letters, which fixes the r1 failure. The blade angles up and away, out of the top-right corner, and no body, chest or cloth touches it. There is no blood and no red. Acceptable with reservations. It is a floor-level upward view with jackfruit leaves black against a starry night sky and lamp glow, and it keeps screen direction (sanctum left, jackfruit right). v01 (the only candidate): Varma, kneeling at right, is drawn with the young clean-shaven face of the temple-priest sheet: no moustache, white ash stripes and a red dot on the brow. decisions.correction: Varma, kneeling back from the chaver's body on the right of the courtyard, must have the face from the varma-v1 sheet: a thick black curled moustache, a mature man in his thirties with a heavier build, black hair gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, one gold chain and a cream mundu with a thin gold border. He must NOT have the young clean-shaven face of the temple-priest sheet. There are no ash stripes and no red dot on his brow, only a line of white sandal paste, smeared and broken (no blood). Keep everything else exactly as it worked: the high angle from inside the jackfruit canopy; the chaver face down on the flags, bare-chested with no blood; Nagoji kneeling at left-centre with the dagger lowered in his left hand, held away from his body, and his right arm hanging; the old priest's arm locked around the heir in the sanctum doorway beside the pillar; the dog flattened against the far wall; and clear wall and foliage across the top of the frame for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor: a second, older arm in a white cloth with a red border enters at the left edge. It reads as the chaver's arm, which the script does not ask for. v01 (the only candidate) shows blood, which the script forbids for this panel ('No blood rendered'). Varma's brow cut is a red gash, and red runs from the corner of his lip. decisions.correction: Draw no blood anywhere: no red cut, drip, trickle or smear on either man. Show Varma's injury only through the line of white sandal paste across his brow, cracked and split apart by a cut drawn in ink only (no red), and a visibly swollen lower lip. Keep what worked: the two-shot with Varma on the left and Nagoji on the right getting to his feet; Nagoji's high topknot with grey temples, moustache, clean chin, silver chain and gold ear stud; Varma's moustache, pearl earring and one gold chain; the sanctum, jasmine and niche lamps behind; the jackfruit tree at right; and the plain upper wall clear for two short balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's black hair is wavy and gathered in a knot at the back of his head rather than combed sleek into a knot above the LEFT ear. decisions.correction: The chaver's body lies face down on the flags at the lower left, a little distance from the tree. decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): Varma at screen left does not match his sheet. Acceptable. The staging is right: Varma on the left, Nagoji on the right, and Nagoji's RIGHT shoulder bound. Minor: Varma's upper cloth hangs from his left shoulder instead of the injured right one, and he rests his chin on his right hand. The stitched cut runs up into his hairline. v01 (only candidate): Nagoji is in his captivity costume, a ragged ochre sleeveless tunic with a red sash. decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Ramayyan seated at left by the low table, turned toward Nagoji with his stylus pointing at him and a palm-leaf bundle in his other hand; Varma seated behind the table in the middle; Nagoji seated cross-legged on the mat at right, in profile facing left; the brass open-wick lamp and cups on the table; and the open doorway onto the torchlit courtyard with horses picketed in a line. His long curly black hair is gathered into a high Kerala topknot on the crown with first grey at the temples, not hanging loose. A fine silver chain of office hangs around his neck as a necklace, never a heavy iron chain, shackle or links across his body. decisions.issues: Minor: the upper cloth hangs from Varma's left shoulder, not the injured right one. He stands just inside, beside the open doorway, rather than in it. Framing differs from the script. Ramayyan is a sharp, full mid-ground figure with his hand raised, not a blurred hand in the foreground, and the head shake reads as a sideways turn. decisions.issues: Minor issues only. The beat is correct: his right upper arm is bandaged and the forearm lies across his body, and his wrapped left hand grips the silver chain. Clean. This is a tight insert of Ramayyan's hands, with the stylus cutting faint lamplit grooves into a palm leaf on the low table. The marks are abstract lines with no pseudo-text. Both hands have sound anatomy, the cloth is plain white, and the brass open-wick lamp, cup and doorway onto the torchlit picketed horses match the room. Only his chin shows at the top edge, so the tail points off-panel upward. The plain wall at upper middle-right leaves room for the short balloon.

v01 (only candidate) misses the script's explicit beat that both men toast left-handed. Varma's torso faces the viewer, and the arm holding his cup comes from his image-left shoulder, the one under the cream shoulder cloth. That is his injured RIGHT arm, swung across his chest in a full toast. Nagoji correctly toasts with his wrapped LEFT hand across his body. But his RIGHT arm is unbound and hanging bare, while a bandage wraps his LEFT upper arm, which breaks the bible row (right shoulder bound). The brand on his left forearm is drawn as a dark round tattoo-like stamp, not a pale puckered patch. What works: the cups meeting over the lamp, Varma's one-eye wince mid-laugh with a stitched brow, his pearl drop earrings and gold bead chain, Nagoji's face, stud, topknot and silver chain, the torchlit horses through the doorway, and clear upper wall and sky for lettering.
decisions.correction: Both men toast LEFT-handed. Varma sits on the left facing right. He raises his cup in his LEFT hand, the arm on the side of his body nearer Nagoji. His RIGHT arm, under the cream cloth draped over his injured right shoulder, stays lowered and still in his lap and does not hold a cup. Nagoji sits on the right facing left. He raises his cup in his LEFT hand, its palm wrapped in clean linen, crossing in front of his body. His RIGHT arm, the one on the side of his body nearer Varma, is folded across his chest in a cream cloth sling knotted over his right shoulder. There is no bandage on his left upper arm. Draw the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm as a pale puckered patch of raised ridges, not a dark round stamp or tattoo. Keep everything else that worked: the two brass cups meeting large above the open-wick lamp at the centre of the frame, Varma wincing mid-laugh with one eye squeezed shut, the small stitched cut on his brow, his pearl drop earrings, one gold bead chain and bare head with his hair knotted up. Keep Nagoji's high topknot, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain, thick curled moustache and clean chin, the open doorway onto the torchlit courtyard with picketed horses, and the plain upper wall and dark sky for lettering.

decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji has no visible silver chain of office, and no grey at the temples, though both show in 14.2. Everything else is right. The courtyard has laterite walls, a tiled gatehouse, horses picketed and hard daylight. The right arm is in a cloth sling and the left palm is wrapped. He has the moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small gold stud and a high topknot. Padmini matches her sheet: grey threading her black hair, gold, the walking stick planted and the cream sari. Hands are sound. Open blue sky across the top centre and top right holds the caption and both balloons.

Minor: a white cloth wrap on Nagoji's right wrist, although the script says no bandage. It reads as a rider's wrist wrap, not an injury. The chain of office is drawn dark steel-grey rather than bright silver. Otherwise right: the column of white-turbaned, white-clad lancers rides on a palm-lined coastal track under a heavy monsoon sky. The red standard with the silver conch carries no writing. Nagoji leads on Kayal: bay, black mane, ochre quilted pad, no white markings. He has the high topknot with grey temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, talwar hilt and shoulder cloth, with no sling or turban. The dark sky at upper right and upper centre is clear for both captions.

Minor only. The water runs to the horses' bellies rather than their knees. The ear ornament is a small round gold bead on the lobe, which reads as a stud. The column is all white-turbaned riders, with none of the Maravar or Madurai variety from 14.2 (14.3 does not require it). Otherwise clean: Nagoji has a high topknot with grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the silver chain and a shoulder cloth, with no turban, sling or bandage. Kayal is a bay with a black mane and no white markings. The column fords one way at dusk toward the far bank. There is no painted text. The open sky at upper right suits caption 0 and the calm water band along the bottom suits the closing caption 1. The look matches 14.2 (same costume and mare).
